utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The proceedings are continuing under Rule 15 bis. It's cross-examination, isn't it? Ms. Reidy, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. If I just may, Your Honours. I have received back the revised translation of P130 ID. That is with the stamp that was on it now fully translated, and I just may suggest that perhaps we would enter is this into evidence and give an exhibit number so that if it is raised in cross, that we are actually using the final version. And I've given the version with the stamp translated to Defence counsel this morning, and I've left copies for the Bench and the Registry, with the Registry officer this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any objection now that it's translated? I see none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, we don't have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have it -- can we have the formal number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. It's P130 and P130 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If it pleases, before my colleague Mr. Krgovic continues his cross-examination, I, on behalf of all Defence counsel, have to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to one issue. Yesterday we were informed by our colleagues from the Prosecution that there will be some changes in order of appearance of some witnesses. Actually, we are expecting, according to their order, to the order that they gave us of appearance, that after this witness, Witness Bobic, Edina and witness Bobic, Kemal will testify before this Tribunal. Then yesterday they informed us that there are some changes and that after this witness there is Witness A, who will give his testimony, and they expect it to be on Monday. What I would like to inform the Trial Chamber is that we still have not received the B/C/S version of his statement according to Rule 92 bis. Speaking now about all the possibilities and all the issues that this raises, we do believe that if they give us tomorrow, so it means on Friday, the B/C/S version, and since we cannot contact with our clients and get necessary instructions, because the Detention Unit is not working on Saturday and Sunday, I believe that we will not be ready for this witness, actually, that we will not have enough time according to Rule 21 of the Statute of the Tribunal. So I would like just to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber that we do not have B/C/S version so we can get instructions from our clients. I mean, we did some draft translation, but it is not good enough for our clients to give instructions to us regarding Witness A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. What is the position?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The position, Your Honours, is that the Defence is correct insofar as they don't have a B/C/S version. They have had for a number of weeks the English version. It's a very, very long statement. It was sent -- we got it translated, and it needed to be revised before it was disclosed, so that the Defence wouldn't have a poor quality translation. And that revision process is not finished of the B/C/S version because the statement is of some length. So although they've had the English version for a number of weeks, if the lack of a B/C/S version is problematic to the Defence, then we would simply call Witness A viva voce when he arrives. I don't think that we have any alternative. We will get the translation to them as soon as we have it, but it has been taking a long time because of the length of the statement, and as I said, we needed to revise it to ensure the quality was of sufficient standard that we wouldn't get complaints from Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, further to what Ms. Reidy said, it is not disputed that we received the English version, the English draft versions, and we talked about that with our clients and went over that when we visited them in the Detention Unit, but our clients do wish to have B/C/S draft versions with them so that they can, during their free time, go over those statements. I think it's a fundamental right of every accused to have those statements, and it is also the obligation of the other side to provide everything to the accused in the language that the accused understands. Our clients should be able to have that statement and be able to use it in his spare time. That's the main problem that we have with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not denying counsel rights to request a B/C/S version. I'm simply stating that in the time frame, with the length of the document, it's not been possible, and once we have it available, once it becomes in any form ready to disclose, we'll disclose it. We're not with holding it. It's just with the length of the statement, it's taken that long time to be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll see. Let's proceed with the cross-examination in the meantime. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, as I'm taking the Witness A, I need to know how I'm going to deal with him, because, of course, if I -- if he's going to be done in the usual manner, viva voce, in order to simply save time, then I'll prepare accordingly, and if not, I won't. So now, he's coming in I think on Friday, and I'm seeing him on the weekend, so I would like to know -- not necessarily now, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But at a stage in the proceedings. MR. DI FAZIO: But at some stage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we rise. MR. DI FAZIO: Before we rise, and perhaps if possible today, if not, tomorrow, so that I can prepare accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber will deal with that at a later stage. Let's continue with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Krgovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 31 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, could the statement be given to the witness, please, the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on the 16th of April you moved your family to Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further on, you said that you observed that Serb families moved their children out of town. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Muslims and Croats also moved their families out of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he moved his family out of Bosanski Samac before April 16th?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that his brother remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he moved his son out of Bosanski Samac? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His son left after the incident that took place before the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic and Izet Izetbegovic are high officials of the SDA party in Bosanski Samac, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And both of them are Muslims, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the Bicic brothers, Muhamed and Hasan?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that they moved their families out of Bosanski Samac before the 16th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan Lukac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he also moved his family out of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, based on your testimony, I concluded that your wife, upon leaving Bosanski Samac on the 16th of April, returned to Bosanski Samac later on, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After nine days, when I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So she came back normally from Gradacac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she entered Bosanski Samac without any hindrance?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she did, but she couldn't leave afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I will put some questions to you regarding your exchange. That's paragraph 118, 119, and 120. You were exchanged on the 26th of May, 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the first exchange between Bosanski Samac and Orasje, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 120, you stated, and I will read these two sentences to you: "We were put on a truck and brought to Zasavica. There were Serbs there who were exchanged for us. It was organised by the ICRC." Is it correct, this what I just read to you out from your statement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The Serbs were not on that side. They were all around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this part here, where it says that it was all organised by the ICRC, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll look at your exchange in a chronological order, and I'll put some questions to you so that we can explain this entire procedure to the Trial Chamber in some more detail. In paragraph 119, you explained how the ICRC took statements from you at the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when did this take place? On the day you were exchanged or on the day when you were transferred from the elementary school to the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the day of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were called to give a statement on behalf of the representatives of the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A lady --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting, but just for the clarification of the transcript, on page 7 -- it escaped me already, but you said -- in any event, you said that this was the first exchange between Bosanski Samac and Orasje. That can't be true. He went to Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's right. He went to Odzak, but the exchange was between the municipality of Orasje and municipality of Bosanski Samac. The commission was in Orasje, but the municipality is that of Odzak. So it was the municipality of Odzak, and the commission was from Odzak. I am correcting myself here. So the exchange was between the Serb and the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, there was a woman there, a foreigner, and a man, who was also a foreigner?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the interpreter was not a foreigner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This lady, if you remember, was called Katherine.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what she was called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She asked you whether you wanted to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpreter asked me. I don't know the name of the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But she gave instructions to the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you gave your statement by the table at the elementary school, in the hallway, there were no local Serbs present there, were they?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the interpreter was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to local Serbs. There were no local Serbs from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were guards some one metre away from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you gave all the information that they required?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they recorded that information?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is how I was registered with the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, you were taken on the trucks to the location of the exchange?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before that, I was told that I had to accept to be exchanged or else I would be killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were told this by Stiv Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that this was an exchange 100 people on one side to be exchanged for 100 people on the other side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I learned that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 100 people were taken to the exchange location?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I was in the last truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That same woman was the first one to cross across the River Bosna in a boat?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were already on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This lady --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Somebody else was on the other side, because the lady remained on this side while we were crossing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she was there the entire time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the entire time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stood by the truck?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were on the truck. We were not allowed to get off the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there were members of the army and snipers on the other side, on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that, but I saw them on this side. I could see clearly from the truck that they were lying down with snipers and machine-guns, all around us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were on the trucks and not far from the trucks was a table, where the representative of the ICRC sat?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the table was some distance away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was the table from the truck?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some 100 or 200 metres. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And nobody was allowed to approach the table until his or her name was called out?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Miroslav Tadic had to call your name, and then you were allowed to get off the truck, and we went in groups of five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went in groups of five or six, approached the table, and then once again gave a statement to the representative of the ICRC as to whether you wanted to be exchanged or not?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't follow that procedure. I went straight to the boat, because prior to that I had already stated that I wanted to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear -- did you see other people approaching the table and giving their statements?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the last one to be exchanged, and none of the five of us went to give another statement about the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you're over lapping. The interpreter is overworked. You're overlapping. So please do pause. And the witness should also pause after listening to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I would kindly ask you to wait for me to finish my question, then wait another two seconds, and then give your answer, so that we do not overlap, for the benefit of the interpreters. Did you see anybody from previous groups remaining by the table?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that. All I cared about is getting on the boat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you wanted to get on the boat as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, my client claims that on that occasion, ten of your co-citizens, fellow citizens, did not want to cross to the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said in my statement that the exchange was discontinued for some time. At the time, I didn't know why it was so, but I had heard that if somebody was to give up, then the exchange would be completely discontinued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was whether you saw that ten of your fellow citizens did not cross to the other side and that they said to the representative of the ICRC that they do not want to be exchanged and go to the other side.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 117, you said that you knew most of the Croats who were in the so-called isolation. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to introduce a document now. It is a list for exchange on the 25th of May, 1992, the exchange in which this witness participated and was exchanged. I have an English translation as well here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- the Prosecution be given a copy? We were given a number of documents which were intended to be introduced, so I don't know which one of them is now being put into evidence. But you've given me a number of documents, Mr. Lukic, and they're all lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was given to the case manager yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, one of several documents, which is just what I'm trying to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you put on the ELMO for our client.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, do you see your name on this list? Please look at number 3.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, sir, that you were the only Muslim that was exchanged on that day. Can you please read the name under number 1.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was the only Muslim from Bosanski Samac municipality. Salkanovic, Kemo under number 1 is not from Bosanski Samac. He is not from our municipality. He was brought there on the day of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's a Muslim, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please read the name under number 35. Can you tell us the name of that person, item 35?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, 35.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blaskic, Ilija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't cross to the other side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it say by his name?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here "refused."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "refused." I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this man?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read the name under number 65.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petric Marko, "refused." That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he didn't cross to the other side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. I couldn't have known everybody in the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at number 77 on the second page. Please read the name.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Barisic Ivo, "refused." There's no date of his A, concerning his age. He's an older person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he didn't cross?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he crossed or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read under number 24. What is the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petric Ivo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he didn't cross?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know -- I don't know who crossed and did not.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know all these people. They're old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw in isolation that they were all old people. I only knew some people. Most of these people were old, 60, 70, and more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see whether all elderly people crossed or not?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that I didn't see whether everybody had crossed or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read out number 39, the name of the person?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pejic Tadija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't cross?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 49.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petric Andrija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A person worked as a telephone operator at the post office. Do you know he didn't cross?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 55, please read the name.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stazic Ilija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know he didn't cross?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 56, what is the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cvitkusic Simo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he didn't cross over?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please turn to the next page, number 96. What is the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pranjic Stjepan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he didn't cross?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask: This list which was read out by Miroslav Tadic, in front of the truck, is that a list of people who earlier applied for the exchange?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who applied earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said earlier in the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with the people on the truck, whether they applied for the exchange in the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have contact with others earlier. I was shut up in a classroom, and only in the -- then in the gym, I saw the people in the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would submit this list as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I do have a number of problems with this document. Unlike a lot of the lists of persons for exchange, this particular one bears no signature, no stamp, nothing that indicates who drew up this list, or in fact that it's ever anything more than a draft or anything like that. There are then a number of annotations on it, and, in particular, Defence counsel has, I can tell from this line of questioning, been suggesting that there are certain annotations against, for example, I think, number 39. Now, there is something very, very faded on the copy that I have beside 39 but on the translation you can see there's nothing translated in the English version against 39, and that goes for a number of allegations that the counsel has put to the witness. Now, the witness has not been able to provide -- I didn't interrupt because I wanted to see if the witness could help provide personal knowledge about this, and he said on every occasion, "I didn't know this person. I don't know if they crossed or not. I don't know whether they crossed." So he's not been able to corroborate anything that Defence counsel has put to him. So I let it go to the end to see if we could get any idea of whether or not this was a genuine list from the time or whether those annotations mean anything, but I'm afraid that I don't know, for example, if the handwriting in the corner, the one that says "exchanged," could mean that everybody on this list was exchanged. So without that sense, any sort of, I would say, reliability of the document in the absence of a stamp or a signature that we would ask it only to be ID at the moment because this witness has not been able to help us with any of the allegations put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Reidy. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the witness recognised himself and the first person on the list. So this is as far as the recognition goes. Secondly, the document hasn't a seal and a signature because the commission didn't exist yet, and it was organised by the International Red Cross, which was also confirmed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see now the problem you're having, counsel. You're now giving evidence on the matters raised by the Prosecution, and what you should do is actually call evidence, yes? Because the Trial Chamber does agree with the position of the Prosecution that this document cannot be admitted through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, earlier the same documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the explanations you are giving are supposed to come through as evidence. It's true that the only -- the witness has identified his own name as being on the list, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would propose this submitted as evidence, and also for the ID. He has -- the witness -- I would only enter this evidence for identification of the document, and later on we will prove the line of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be marked for identification only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D69/3 ID and D69/3 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to return this list to the witness because I intend to raise a few more questions in connection with the list with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, you can place the list in front of you. It doesn't have to be on the ELMO. Look at this list. Except for you and Salkanovic Kemo do you know anybody else from the list? I'm asking this because you said when you were moved to the secondary school, that you knew most of the Croats.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew most of those who were in the gym room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any of these: Barukcic Nikola? Did he cross over?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Agatic Pero, did he cross over?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prcic Zeljko?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew his father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he cross over?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- yes. MR. DI FAZIO: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrvelj Juraj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel. MR. DI FAZIO: Could we have the number so we can see where in the document the names are? Because each name has a number next to it. Makes it a lot easier

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It makes it easier. Mr. Krgovic, you call out the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, we will have to begin from the beginning. So please read out the number, then the name, and say whether the person went with in the exchange. Number 2?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petric Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The son of Simo. He went across?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Number 4, Agatic Pero. He crossed over with me. Barukcic Nikola, number 5 -- Number 5, Barukcic Nikola, he also crossed over. Number 8, Mrvelj Juraj. He also crossed. 11 and 12 Loncaric Andrija and Loncaric Petar. They also crossed over. Number 16, Pandurevic Bono. He also crossed over. Number 43, Sinkovic Ivo. He also crossed over and I knew him. Number 58, Mikic Ivo. He also crossed over. Brasnic Ivo, number 63. He also crossed over. Number 68, Kljajic Pavo. He also crossed over.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Jasarevic. Could I just clarify one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The last name you mentioned, just for the record, I think it's going to be confusing. You mentioned a Mr. Pavo Kljajic, I think, and you said -- or at least the transcript says it's number 68. On the document I'm looking at, it's at number 67. Is that correct? That's the man you're talking about, number 67, not 68?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 67, Kljajic Pavo. And this is approximately the people I knew who crossed over. I knew them mostly by sight than more personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasarevic. Mr. Jasarevic, this exchange succeeded, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender another document. That is a list of persons which came from the opposite side, namely, from the Croatian side. I also have an English translation of this document. The document has been disclosed to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I was just wondering, because you said that this document was from the Croatian side. What would this witness know about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a document from the Croatian side. It's a list of the people who came from the Croatian side, whether he knows any of them, what they looked like, the age.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, you, as the last one to go in that group of five, you had the opportunity of seeing people who crossed over?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were people on stretchers?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on stretchers, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the people and their age. Here we have mainly elderly people.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have the age of these people on the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we have people who are 1918, 1912, 1915.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the age structure of the people who came over from the other side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, do you remember -- do you recall that in the vehicles which were taking you to Odzak - it means the bus - that there was a few Serbs who were not allowed to cross over?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you find out later that a number of Serbs were not allowed to cross over because a number of Croats did not cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go to the next page. Which is the last number here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the list. Do you know any of these people who crossed over from the other side? Did you recognise any of them? Did you know any of these people from the municipality of Odzak? They were mainly from Dubica?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if they worked with me, but here it's hard to say by the names. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these names of places written next, are all these places in the municipality of Odzak?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at this list and see if you can -- if you know any of these people.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know these people from the other municipality. Only a relatively small number of them worked in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've ended with this document, and Your Honours, I wish to tender this document for evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can see this document bears a signature, although we don't know who of, so I have less concerns about it. Again, I just have doubts about any probative value of it since the witness has not been able to identify someone from the list or comment upon it. So I think it is of little probative value. But it has a signature, so the Bench thinks it's worth admitting, it could be admitted, as I said, but we think it is of little probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The question will be how much weight to be attached to it. Can we have it marked as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D70/3 ter and D70/3. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, only a few more questions concerning your exchange. In paragraph 118, you stated: "I found out that my colleague, a Croat, that he asked that my name be put on the list for exchange when the list was finalised." That was in Slavonski Brod. Tell me: Where is Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it mean that "where the list was finalised"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is where the representative of ICRC were located, namely, in Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you heard that you were placed there on the list?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you were being sought?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that I was being sought out. I didn't even know that anybody was looking for me and making this request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to whom your relative turned on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I will ask you a few questions concerning the exchange of your wife. Your wife was exchanged on the 5th of November, 1992; isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She was exchanged with Jelena Kapetanovic, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. My wife even didn't know Jelena Kapetanovic, at least not well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that she was exchanged with her?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was -- the bus was full. They were packed. I was only looking whether to see -- I can see my wife and children. I didn't look at others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is whether you know that she was exchanged with Jelena Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when Jelena Kapetanovic was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness has already answered that question, and he's being asked again, so I was wondering why. Because he has already given the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to ask whether he knows, whether he claims that she was not exchanged with Jelena Kapetanovic or that he doesn't know about the fact. However, in the last answer, he answered the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, your wife certainly told you about her life in Samac and her attempt for the exchange.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And certainly at the crossover in Dragalici, the UN asked her whether she wanted to cross over to the other side.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask that, but I know that she wanted to cross over to the other side, where I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to reunite?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the exchange took place in Dragalici?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you know, you insisted with the commissions in Croatia that from your exchange, up to the exchange of your wife, during those five months, a number of exchanges took place?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also said that your mother-in-law left with the same -- last -- in one of the last exchanges.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one of the last exchanges in 1993, from Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree if I say that that was on the 24th of December, 1993, for Catholic Christmas?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. As I said, my mother-in-law -- I believe it was the last exchange. An elderly woman, 70-odd years, from Zasavica -- Zasavica camp. She was transferred. Nobody asked where she will be going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the exchange of your wife to the exchange of your mother-in-law, there were at least some ten exchanges?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many exchanges took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, your wife was among the first exchanges?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After seven months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me count the months. You left on the 26th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife -- it's in my statement -- came after the -- seven months after my exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 26th of May, and not 26th of April. That is a correction for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were exchanged -- namely, she was exchanged on the 5th of November, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven months later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It means June, July, August, September, October, November?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I'm wondering why you are going round and round these dates of exchange, the months. There's no dispute. The witness has given the evidence on all these. Why are we going round and round to see how many months after and all that? That can be calculated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness said that between his exchange and that of his wife, seven months passed, which is not true, because it was only five months that passed. And the aim of my cross-examination is to establish with the witness, since he said that his wife was not allowed to be exchanged because he was in the HVO and shot at the Serb side, and the fact is that his wife was in one of the first exchanges, and this is all I'm trying to analyse with the witness. This is why I asked him when he left, when she left, how many exchanges there were between his exchange and that of his wife, and how long the exchanges were going on for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were at least three exchanges between mine and that of my wife, before my wife left the town. I don't know exactly how many, but I know that there was one exchange in July. I know at least that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, so there were at least three exchanges between your exchange and that of your wife?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had to wait for seven months for my wife. I don't know the dates exactly, but my wife did not leave the town for seven months. You have some other kind of list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But she was exchanged even though the Serbs knew that you shot at them, at the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: Who did you see about your wife's exchange? Who did you plead with?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several commissions in Croatia: In Odzak, in Domaljevac. I went to see all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go and see Mijo Matanovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't meet Mijo Matanovic. I went to some offices and there were some names there, but I don't remember any more. I went to the international organisations. I went from Domaljevac to Djakovo by foot, on foot - I'm sorry - because there were no other means of transportation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to see these commissions and put your wife's name down as the name of somebody who wanted to cross to the other side?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When did I do what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you put down your wife's name as somebody who wants to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as I was exchanged and I had the first opportunity to do so, I put her name down for an exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not see that her name was actually put down for the exchange?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was told in the office in Samac that her name was on the list and then that it was erased from the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Did you actually see the name of your wife being put on the list?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I put that name down myself, together with the name of my children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Marko Bozanovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go and see him to urge for your wife to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him, and I asked him to help my wife and children be exchanged. I don't know what function he held at the time, but I knew him, and I asked him to help me get my wife and children exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've finished my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Novic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jasarevic. My name is Sredoje Novic, and on behalf of Mr. Blagoje Simic, I will be putting questions to you. I will kindly ask you to give me yes-or-no answers, if possible; in cases where you don't know the answer, just please say "I don't know." Mr. Jasarevic, can we agree that in the time period between January and April 1992, in Bosanski Samac, there was an increased tension which was expressed, among other things, in the interethnic division among people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you have in mind, interethnic division or division among ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, among the residents, there was an ethnic division?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not on my side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not interested in that. Please answer my questions. Among other things, Serbs frequented Serb cafes, Croats frequented Croatian cafes, and Muslims frequented their own?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you know that immediately prior to the breakout of conflict in April 1992 in Bosanski Samac, the Muslim government in Sarajevo issued an order to organise the Territorial Defence in Bosanski Samac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've got a problem with counsel's question. He talks about the Muslim government in Sarajevo. What Muslim government in Sarajevo? I think -- I mean -- the government that was elected at the time that was operating in Sarajevo? Is he talking about -- I don't know of any official entity called "the Muslim government," and I'd like to have that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. At the material time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope it is a well-established fact that in Sarajevo there was a Croat/Muslim government, and that Serbs were not part of that government, and that that government issued an order to organise Territorial Defence in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have information about the fact that the decision of that government, concerning the organisation of Territorial Defence in Bosanski Samac, was adopted without the approval of the Serb side and led to an increase of tensions?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That decision was issued with the participation of all -- representatives of all three sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I would now like to turn your attention to what you said in paragraph 29.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three representatives in the TO: There was one Croat, one Serb, and one Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask that you instruct the witness to answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said this was the Muslim government. I said it was the government from Sarajevo. And you are now claiming that it was the Muslim government, which didn't even exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please read the text of paragraph 29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate that this may be the first time that counsel is cross-examining here, but he's saying -- he's asking the Bench to instruct the witness to answer questions. I can't follow the cross, with the questions he's trying to pose, the speed it's going. Maybe it's a problem with the interpretation, that the transcript comes a bit later, but I think that at the moment he's being unfair to the witness in suggesting he's not answering a question, when I can't see a question being posed. And maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So far the witness has been answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: My observation is that the counsel is a bit too fast. If counsel can be waiting for interpretation of the answers to be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 29, Mr. Jasarevic, you said: "Shortly before the war ..." Will you please read this out.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Will you please read it out loud. Or shall I read it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here is what I've stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this lead to the increased tensions in the area? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were tensions, but the TO distributed weapons only one day before the attack on Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm asking you, Mr. Jasarevic, is whether what you stated here is true.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Let's turn to another topic. Mr. Jasarevic, when did you join the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member since the time when I finished my mandatory military service, which was in 1972, and then up until the breakout of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what tasks did you have in the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly securing the railway line when Tito's train passed through, and things that had to do with security and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain with the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, until the breakout of war. I didn't really pay attention to the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it until 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I was removed from the reserve force one year before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please: What was your wartime assignment?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wartime assignment was with the civil protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you are still ahead. Can you please pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, can you please tell me: Who was the commander of the reserve police force in Samac while you were on that reserve force?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Ivan Lonac, Ljoljic Mijo

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please slow down. So it was Ivan?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ivan Lonac and Ljoljic Mijo. These are the names I remember. There were other people there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Lonac is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know. All right. We have information that you were issued with a Kalashnikov weapon. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us whether this is true or not. Yes or no. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I object to that.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not -- MR. DI FAZIO: Why is he being asked to repeat what's in his statement? If it's in his statement, counsel can be assured that the Chamber has read it. The Chamber has read it. We know it's there. It's as if he gave evidence in Court. That's, at least, how I understand 92 bis works. So what's the point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Novic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand my learned colleague from the Prosecution; however, I hope that he will have read the statement and seen that the witness did not state that in his statement. So my question is not out of place. This is why I'm asking whether this is true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Paragraph 28 -- perhaps counsel has not read the statement. It says: "We were not supplied with arms until closer to the takeover. I was issued with a weapon and a clip of ammunition, which was given to me by Safet Srna. I never used this weapon, and I returned it immediately. I had it for approximately 24 hours. I had my hunting rifle." It's there in paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still insist to receive an answer. It doesn't say in the statement that the witness had a Kalashnikov weapon. My question was quite precise, and I want to receive a yes-or-no answer. That's all. And I don't see what is contentious here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For the purposes of this case, it's sufficient if the witness has stated that he had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The type of weapon, Your Honours, is quite important for this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the weapons are not the same. A weapon can be a pistol, a weapon can be a cannon, it can also be a Kalashnikov, it can be a sniper. There are many different types of weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but as far as the Trial Chamber is concerned, it is a weapon intended to be used against persons, as opposed to a hunting rifle. I don't think we should be wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If Your Honours believe this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shouldn't be wasting time about these material details which actually do not affect the issues in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may assist, Your Honour. In fact, it is very important. It is of crucial significance, because type of weapon is related to certain documents, exhibits, when we introduced that, in the SDA armed wing in Bosanski Samac. You remember well that there are many lists of members of SDA and the type of the weapon that they were given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But following -- yes. Following the evidence of Mr. Fitozovic, I don't think there is any contention from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but in this particular case, my -- our impression is that this witness is avoiding to say very openly what the type -- it's just one question: What type of weapon you were given? And point. I mean, I don't see any particular reason not to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I don't think it's fair to say that the witness was avoiding to say what type. It's the way the question was put to the witness. If the witness is asked directly: You have stated in your statement that you had a weapon. What type exactly were you issued with? That is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I agree. That can be done. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it's fair to blame the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Jasarevic. In paragraph 28 of your statement, you stated that you had a weapon and that it had been given to you together with a clip of ammunition. Will you please tell the Chamber what type of weapon was given to you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifle. I don't know what type it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I know, and you have stated so yourself, you were qualified even to repair weapons.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't have any further knowledge?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an automatic rifle when I was in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to automatic weapon that you were issued with, you also had a hunting carbine, a hunting rifle, a so-called shotgun?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a shotgun. It wasn't a pump-action gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a pump-action gun?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same type of a rifle?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me: What is of a higher quality out of those two?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shotgun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shotgun. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Your Honours, please. I need to consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, in your statement dated 19th May, 2002, which you gave to the Prosecution, in paragraph 6, you stated that you had two hunting rifles -- you owned two of those. One was a carbine and the other one was a pump-action gun.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never stated that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your statement is not true?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was probably a translation error. Please allow me to finish. I had a hunting rifle, a so-called shotgun, and the second one was a carbine. So those are the two that I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also had a hunting knife with your name engraved?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a hunting knife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did I understand it well that you were also a constructer who constructed a small cannon?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, but I didn't have a cannon. My statement reflects everything about that cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me: What was the mechanism used in that cannon? Was it a water mechanism, air mechanism, or filling mechanism? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, what can be the possible relevance of that? The witness said he made a homemade cannon that fired a cannon ball made of paper used at Ramadan and now we're being asked about the mechanism of that cannon. Who cares? What's the relevance of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If this counsel wants to put to the witness that he had an armaments factory and was producing a production line of cannons that he was producing, howitzers and so on out of his back yard, fine, let him put it to the witness. But what can the mechanism of a cannon used at Ramadan, how can that be relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This cannon that you developed, did it us an explosive charge? Did it use that type of mechanism?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Every cannon uses that type. Mechanism.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You are a locksmith by trade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also had some special skills in working with metals and maintenance and repair of weapons?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any additional weapons in addition to the ones that we just mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please clarify something for us. In your statement that you gave to the Prosecution, on the 3rd, 4th, and 5th of February of 1995, on page 00637808, it says as follows: "A neighbour came to see me in my neighbour's basement and told me that I had to hand over my pistol."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never stated that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You read the statement and signed it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the translation was, but I never stated that I had a pistol or that I turned it over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you -- have you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which statement you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The statement that you gave on the 3rd, 4th, and 5th of February, 1995. Have you signed it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've signed all of my statements. However, I never signed to the fact that I had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would be fair of counsel to show the witness the statement. The statement he's talking about, I don't have here, is an English statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If a witness does sign a statement in English, what happens is the translator is there and reads back to the witness what's in it. Now, a translator may have said -- investigator may have said pistol, may have said back, "your gun." He said, "yes." That's what's in it in general. The witness -- in any of those statements does not read the exact word, you know, which is written, and it's in English, and I think that should be made clear so the Bench understand. And this statement which he read back to himself -- which the witness has read himself in B/C/S does describe how his neighbour came and said they had been looking for weapons. "Please go hand it in in case someone fires at the house," and how the witness went back and handed it in. That's all been explained on the record. So I just want the Bench to understand that that statement from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I apologise yet again to the interpreters. The statement from 1995, the Bench should understand is an English statement and it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps maybe if there is a B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for clarification. We've been through all these explanations. This is a serious criminal proceedings. We have a serious proofs and exhibits here. This witness said, on 1995, and he signed this document, he signed that statement, and he was warned by the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. You have the Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: English version is signed. We have a Serbo-Croat version and there is a chapter about this particular episode.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then why don't we just refer the particular passage to the witness in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to outline the position that our learned friend from the Prosecution tried to, I would say, mess the thing because it is not the explanation whether the translation was right or wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What I'm saying, Mr. Pantelic, is simply put the passage to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. We shall do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Serbo-Croat one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not objecting. It's up to the Bench to evaluate this. I just would like the Bench to be clear what the procedure is with that first statement. The witness was spoken to by an investigator and a field interpreter. The investigator recorded a statement in English. After that process, it would have been just read out to the witness and the witness would sign an English version. The witness will not have seen a B/C/S version because that sort of translation facility is not possible in the field. So I have no objection to putting the -- of course the part of the statement in B/C/S to the witness, let him explain that it wasn't a pistol or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But just so you understand that this witness will not have read that B/C/S statement and signed on that basis. It is something that when it came back in house, it was translated for the purpose of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It was translated for the purposes of disclosure so that the defendants and the Defence counsel would have a B/C/S copy as the Rules require. It's not the copy that the witness ever had in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Defence counsel should put --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a very serious matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Mr. Pantelic. Would you please just put the B/C/S version to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Allow me just one word. This is very serious matter, Your Honour. This witness signed English version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is not contested.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not contested, but our learned friend from the Prosecution tried to explain how they are not ready for -- this is part a indictment, Your Honour. This is a supporting material when the indictment was issued. So it's very serious criminal matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, nobody is disputing that. I've given you instructions. Will you put the B/C/S passage to the witness and let him answer and explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now, which one of you is cross-examining?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm just giving certain procedural explanation to our learned friends from the Prosecutor Bench. I'm just assistant today for the procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but I will not allow --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Like Mr. Di Fazio. Same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So which one is going to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may just interrupt for one second, Mr. Sredoje Novic, because I believe it's now time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And before we go for break I wanted just to inform the Trial Chamber about one position of the Defence. I mean, in less minutes we have discussed issue and we have our final position regarding whether Witness A could testify according to Rule 92 bis or viva voce. And we also have the confirmation from our clients.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Our final position is as follows: If we receive B/C/S version, unsigned, of course, tomorrow, of Witness A, we would kindly ask this Trial Chamber to issue a ruling that we are allowed to visit our clients during weekend, because we need some sort of permission of the Trial Chamber because otherwise we couldn't go and visit them in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This case will be ready to proceed under 92 bis with Witness A, on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We will take our break and continue the 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Once we start now, we will not take our usual break at 12.30. We shall continue up to 12.45 and break off for the day, because the Judges have meetings for other pre-trial cases at 1.00. And I'm given to understand that the interpreters are willing to go on up to 12.45, and I'm grateful for their understanding. The Trial Chamber was also informed by the Registry and the Detention Unit that actually the counsel are allowed to visit their clients from 0900 Monday to Friday up to about 1645.
